findings.message: Tested 64 of 280 overlapping part pairs: 69 involve parts that could not be measured, 147 were beyond the analysis budget (64 booleans, 128 solids). Unreached pairs were not examined; the most overlapping bounding boxes were tested first.

4 part-volume measurements were unavailable. 4 because a valid closed solid could not be measured (Not manifold): "Roadway", "Deck_Mesh_Roadbed", "SuspendersWest_Mesh_RopePairs", "SuspendersEast_Mesh_RopePairs". 69 overlapping part pairs include one of these parts and were not measured. These parts are not certified clear.
Open surface "SuspendersWest_Mesh_RopePairs" reaches 0.2030 m inside solid "MainCableWest_Mesh_ContinuousCable": 64 of 252 sampled vertices lie deeper inside it than the 0.005 m contact tolerance.
findings.repairText: A positive here is not a defect. Most are intentional: a fitting set into a structural shell -- a lamp recess in a hull, a strut landing, a ridge into a cap -- puts shell vertices inside the solid by design, exactly as a bolt in a hole shares volume. Review the ones you did not intend, such as a cloth crossing a wall or a canopy pierced by a mast, and move the surface clear or cut it back to the solid. Vertices are the samples, so a solid thinner than this surface’s facet spacing can pass between two of them.

metrics.partVolumeScope: Visible static closed mesh pairs, except alternates on different LOD levels; excludes intra-mesh intersections, motion, open surfaces and usable passage space. Positive overlap may be intentional.
metrics.openSurfaceScope: Visible static open surfaces sampled at their vertices against visible static closed solids, except alternates on different LOD levels; excludes open-vs-open pairs, motion, and any solid thinner than the sampled surface's facet spacing. Penetration within the contact tolerance is treated as intended contact, and penetration beyond it may still be intentional, as a fitting socketed into a shell is.
